extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy, theology, and metaphysics (scholars and educated general readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and tests for assessing ultimate religious and scientific ideas (e.g., hypotheses about origin, First Cause, space and time), focusing on conceivability, logical coherence, and representability in thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceivability as the primary test
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not a question of probability, or credibility, but of conceivability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats conceivability (whether an account can be represented in thought) as the decisive criterion: hypotheses that cannot be conceived are deemed untenable regardless of their asserted probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must enable conception of origin of matter
rubrics_metrics.description: "The production of matter out of nothing is the real mystery, which neither this simile nor any other enables us to conceive; and a simile which does not enable us to conceive this, may just as well be dispensed with."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A theory of creation that fails to help us conceive how matter could arise from nothing is judged worthless; evaluators should ask whether the hypothesis truly renders the core mystery intelligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceivability of creation of space
rubrics_metrics.description: If the non-existence of space is absolutely inconceivable, then, necessarily, its creation is absolutely inconceivable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorists must account for whether their hypothesis implies the prior non-existence of space; if non-existence of space cannot be represented in thought, positing its creation is incoherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids infinite regress of external agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation by external agency ... commits us to an infinite series of such agencies, and even then leaves us where we were.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explanation that invokes an external creator should be checked for committing to an endless chain of causes; if it does, it fails as a genuine resolution of origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does not covertly assume self-existence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever agrees that the atheistic hypothesis is untenable because it involves the impossible idea of self-existence, must perforce admit that the theistic hypothesis is untenable if it contains the same impossible idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect theories for hidden assumptions of self-existence (of matter, creator, or space). Any hypothesis that rests on the idea of an uncaused self-existent entity is criticized as rigorously inconceivable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability in thought (mental coherence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiment proves that the elements of these hypotheses cannot even be put together in consciousness; and we can entertain them only ... by abstaining from the endeavour to render them into actual thoughts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A satisfactory hypothesis must be representable as an integrated thought; if its elements cannot be coherently combined in consciousness, it functions only as a pseud-idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject pseud-ideas / symbolic but illegitimate conceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: They severally involve symbolic conceptions of the illegitimate and illusive kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish genuine conceptual content from symbolic or pseud-ideas that only appear intelligible by avoiding rigorous thought; such symbolic constructs are not acceptable as real explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mutual contradiction among essential attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: "But these three conceptions, the Cause, the Absolute, the Infinite, all equally indispensable, do they not imply contradiction to each other, when viewed in conjunction, as attributes of one and the same Being?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attributing multiple ultimate properties (e.g., Cause, Absolute, Infinite) to a single being, check for incompatibilities (e.g., a cause presupposes relation, the absolute implies absence of relation). Coherence requires that these attributes not contradict one another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes assigned must be conceptually compatible (e.g., causation vs absoluteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: "A Cause cannot, as such, be absolute: the Absolute cannot, as such, be a cause. The cause, as such, exists only in relation to its effect: the conception of the Absolute implies a possible existence out of all relation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether attributing causality to an absolute (or absoluteness to a cause) creates category contradictions; theories should not conflate relational and non-relational predicates without addressing the logical consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of divine attributes (power, goodness, justice, mercy, wisdom, freedom)
rubrics_metrics.description: "How, for example, can Infinite Power be able to do all things, and yet Infinite Goodness be unable to do evil? How can Infinite Justice exact the utmost penalty for every sin, and yet Infinite Mercy pardon the sinner? How can Infinite Wisdom know all that is to come, and yet Infinite Freedom be at liberty to do or to forbear?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a hypothesis attributes multiple 'infinite' properties to a deity or ultimate, test whether those properties are mutually reconcilable; apparent contradictions among attributes indicate conceptual failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for genesis of the relative from the absolute
rubrics_metrics.description: We have done nothing towards explaining how the absolute can give rise to the relative, the infinite to the finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A theory that posits an absolute must provide a coherent account of how finite, relative phenomena arise from it; failing to bridge that explanatory gap is a serious defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid representing 'becoming' as a self-contradictory mental object
rubrics_metrics.description: "To think of it in the act of becoming, in the progress from not being into being, is to think that which, in the very thought, annihilates itself."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorists should not rely on conceiving entities as passing from non-existence into existence in thought, because insofar as we think them we already conceive them as existing; the notion of 'becoming' requires careful treatment to avoid this paradox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious creeds as theories of original causation (explanatory claim must be explicit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaving out the accompanying moral code ... a religious creed is definable as a theory of original causation. Now every theory tacitly asserts two things: firstly, that there is something to be explained; secondly, that such and such is the explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a creed or theory, identify (a) what is asserted to need explanation, and (b) the proposed explanatory mechanism; clarity about these two parts is necessary for assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and seek the common abstract element underlying conflicting beliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: We have arrived at a truth underlying even the grossest superstitions ... the vital element in all religions ... is that the Power which the Universe manifests to us is utterly inscrutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques should search for the abstract kernel common to divergent beliefs (e.g., recognition of inscrutability) and assess whether that abstract claim survives rigorous analysis even when particular solutions fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid category mistakes about Space and Time (attributes and entities)
rubrics_metrics.description: To say that Space and Time exist objectively, is to say that they are entities. ... To be conceived at all, a thing must be conceived as having attributes. What now are the attributes of Space? ... to say that Space is extended, is to say that Space occupies Space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses about space and time must avoid attributing categories (like 'extension') to them in ways that create circular or category-confused statements (e.g., 'space is extended' = 'space occupies space'). Explanations should respect the logical conditions for attributing characteristics to entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for limits/limitlessness and divisibility consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: All entities which we actually know as such, are limited; and even if we suppose ... some unlimited entity, we of necessity ... separate it from the class of limited entities. But of Space and Time we cannot assert either limitation or the absence of limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any account of space/time must confront the paradoxes of limit and limitlessness (e.g., inability to imagine unbounded space or a limit to divisibility); a satisfactory theory should not leave these contradictions unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the direct testimony of consciousness regarding objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct testimony of consciousness is, that Time and Space are not within but without the mind; and so absolutely independent of it that they cannot be conceived to become non-existent even were the mind to become non-existent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing that space/time are subjective (forms of intellect), reconcile this with the immediate, inescapable experiential testimony that they appear as external; theories conflicting with direct consciousness require special justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid self-referential contradictions (form of thought cannot also be matter of thought)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Space and Time are the conditions under which we think, then when we think of Space and Time themselves, our thoughts must be unconditioned; and if there can thus be unconditioned thoughts, what becomes of the theory?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not posit that the conditions of thought (forms) can themselves be thought without undermining the claim; avoid explanations that are self-defeating by making the explanans logically incompatible with the act of explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnose hypotheses as 'wholly incomprehensible' when irresolvable
rubrics_metrics.description: It results therefore that Space and Time are wholly incomprehensible. The immediate knowledge which we seem to have of them, proves, when examined, to be total ignorance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hypothesis consistently leads to irresolvable contradictions or category mistakes under analysis, the honest conclusion is that the subject may be presently incomprehensible; evaluators should be willing to acknowledge conceptual limits rather than force inadequate accounts.
